changes.after:
The decider's API: create a run, send one request or a batch, cancel, close. It chooses the provider from the model table and hands the request to whichever shape implements `Decision`; it contains no provider-specific line itself. Tools reach every provider through this one type. Nothing is written new; the prompt lookup from m-4 lands here.

## Deliverables
1. M5-1 sc-decision-runner: apply the corresponding verbatim inventory/change section in design.
2. M5-2 Update crates/decidr/tests/cli.rs to call Run from sc-decision-runner after its move, keeping the CLI assertions (REQ-SAG-0501, REQ-SAG-0701).

Architecture placement (ANC-021; ADR-SAG-0004 v0.5.0): the changes land in `sc-decision-runner`, layer 3, the lowest shared layer for the decision run/send/batch/cancel API because all decision tools reach providers through this runner above the API-shape crates and below their thin public surfaces.

changes.after:
After this sprint, adding a provider or a model is a line of configuration and no Rust change. The compiled-in table becomes the default configuration value, so today's behaviour is the default and every row can be overridden or added to. Settings become one typed struct, so adding a setting is adding a field, and serde does the validation that 150 lines do by hand today. The sprint deletes more than it adds.

## Deliverables
1. M7-1 sc-agent-config typed settings and provider/model rows: apply the corresponding verbatim inventory/change section in design.
2. M7-2 Update sc-agent-py provider_keys to read the configured provider entries in place of the deleted PROVIDERS table, preserving the Python result shape (REQ-SAG-0401, REQ-SAG-0503, ADR-SAG-0005).

Architecture placement (ANC-021; ADR-SAG-0004 v0.5.0): configuration changes land in `sc-agent-config`, layer 1, the lowest shared layer for typed settings and provider/model rows because every launcher needs the same configuration rather than its own Rust provider table.

The `jev` default selects the newest Jev model unless configuration sets another default (ANC-001); defaults contain no hard-coded local-model row, and local-model URL and model id come only from configuration (ANC-022). Related configuration values flow together as the same typed `Settings` struct rather than repeated method parameters (ANC-008). Any tests changed here drive their logic with controlled inputs and do not depend on races, wall-clock timing, sleeps, event-loop ordering or system load (ANC-017).

changes.after:
Sessions go to one SQLite database per repository, written through one crate. A request is stored once and each model's reply is a row that points to it, so the same request sent to five models is one message and five responses, and the cache is one indexed read. Any tool adds its own tables by handing its SQL to the same `open` call; the core schema does not change when a tool is added. The JSONL writer and its global lock are deleted.

## Deliverables
1. M8-1 sc-agent-schema session records and SQL: apply the corresponding verbatim inventory/change section in design.
2. M8-2 sc-agent-sqlite persistence and cache: apply the corresponding verbatim inventory/change section in design.
3. M8-3 sc-agent-log writer replacement: apply the corresponding verbatim inventory/change section in design.
4. M8-4 Update tests/contract/ and crates/sc-agent-py/tests/loopback.py session assertions to read the SQLite sessions and run links instead of sessions.jsonl/runs.jsonl, preserving their existing behavior checks (REQ-SAG-0004, REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0701, ADR-SAG-0019).

Architecture placement (ANC-021; ADR-SAG-0004 v0.5.0): these changes land in `sc-agent-schema`, `sc-agent-sqlite` and `sc-agent-log`, layer 1, the lowest shared layer for session records, SQL, persistence and writing because all tools store sessions through the same core crates rather than duplicating storage in their APIs.


`sc-agent-schema` holds only record structs, literal SQL and their convenience methods, with no SQLite dependency or upgrade code, and defines all core table SQL exclusively (ANC-025, ANC-026). `messages` stores each request once by sha256 and `responses` references that request; cache lookup uses request sha256 and model alone, never run_id (ANC-027, ANC-028). Each tool supplies its own `Schema.owner`, `major` and `migrations` independently of the core version, and no table definition lives in `sc-agent-py` (ANC-032).
